concepts.explanation: The money you start with before any growth.
concepts.label: Principal

concepts.explanation: The yearly percent your savings earn.
concepts.label: Interest rate

concepts.explanation: Interest paid only on the starting sum each year.
concepts.label: Simple interest

concepts.explanation: Interest paid on the sum plus past earnings.
concepts.label: Compounding

concepts.explanation: Money you add on a regular schedule.
concepts.label: Contribution

concepts.explanation: The number of years your money keeps growing.
concepts.label: Time

concepts.explanation: Growth that builds on all previous growth.
concepts.label: Snowball effect

concepts.explanation: The final balance after many years of growth.
concepts.label: Future balance

interaction_type: Compare simple and compound growth with your own numbers
summary: Earnings rejoin your balance each year, so growth builds on growth and time becomes the most powerful ingredient.
